Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: comic-script
Version: 2.3.2

The skill is a straightforward utility for generating comic script templates and writing tips. The core logic in `scripts/comic.sh` uses an inline Python script to print text-based storyboards, character sheets, and layout advice to the console; it contains no network activity, file system modifications, or access to sensitive environment variables.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose (generating comic/storyboard templates) and contains only a small local script that prints templates; nothing appears to access secrets or network resources.

One minor inconsistency: the script invokes python3 but the skill metadata lists no required binaries; declaring python3 as a required binary would be appropriate.

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: a small local CLI that prints comic/storyboard templates. Before installing or running it:
- Note the included scripts/comic.sh calls python3; ensure python3 is present or add it to required binaries.
- Inspect the script locally (it’s short and readable) before executing to confirm you’re comfortable running it.
- The package has no declared homepage/source; the SKILL.md references bytesagain.com—if provenance matters, verify the author/site independently.
- Because the platform allows autonomous invocation by default, consider whether you want the agent to run the skill without prompting; disable autonomous invocation if you prefer manual control.
